text:
alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing a weird spike in notify fanout for SLO alerts when tenants have per-tenant quota overrides. One tenant sent a single breach but we spun up 12 notify webhook calls and a fallback email cascade.

jamal: ugh. repro steps? any traces?

alex: repro: create SLO with notify_policy {tier: 'primary', fallbacks: ['email', 'pager']} + tenant override quota=high. Then trigger a breach (low cardinality). Logs: `notify.fanout.count=12`, `notify.retry.attempts=3` for each.

jamal: looks like our fanout loop doesn't early-exit when quota=override and notify target deduping fails. Proposed quick fix: add per-request cap (max_fanout=4) + metric emit for capped events.

sophie: UI question — if we cap at 4, product will want to show that to users. Can we surface "estimated notification reach" on the SLO card? Also need copy for canary rollouts.

maria: telemetry ask: can we emit `slo.notify.fanout.size`, `slo.notify.capped`, and `slo.notify.estimated_cost_usd`? Need those to build a dashboard and chargeback. Link to draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/notify-fanout

ops-bot: deploy:notify-service v2.14 started (canary=5%) — trace id 0x7f3c.

jamal: implementation note: adding a hard cap is easy, but we should also consider a graceful soft-mode: by default cap but queue remainder for low-priority tenants. That avoids missed important fallbacks.

alex: +1 to soft-mode. Also propose a sampling layer: compact identical webhook targets into one call with a dedupe header, e.g.:

```
POST /internal/notify
{
  "targets": ["hook://a","hook://a","email://oncall"],
  "dedupe": true
}
```

jamal: API nit: don't mix dedupe boolean; prefer `targets: [{url, dedupe_group}]` so we can shard later. But that adds schema churn.

sophie: from UX POV: if we change API we need to coordinate with Dedicated/Private customers (they deploy on-prem). Can we feature-flag the API change and default to old behavior for Private?

maria: for telemetry dashboards we also need tracing. Please ensure each notify attempt emits `trace_id` that maps to the breach event. Otherwise correlation is painful.

tyler: operational concern — cost. If we do per-tenant estimated_cost_usd, we should surface an alert to billing when weekly notify spend > $X. Otherwise we will blow budgets silently.

jamal: action plan I'm taking: open RFC with two proposals (A: hard cap+metrics, B: cap+queue+dedupe API). Will include perf/back-of-envelope cost. I'll ping infra for canary.

sophie: I'll mock the "estimated reach/cost" UI and a tiny affordance that explains soft-cap behavior.

alex: I'll add the telemetry spans and add `slo.notify.capped=true` when cap hits. Also log the tenant id and breach id.

maria: leaving a TODO for dashboards + alert: `notify.fanout.capped_rate > 0.5` for 24h -> paging to eng-platform oncall.

tyler: sounds good. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: jira: ENG-1427 created by jamal - "notify fanout: cap + dedupe RFC"

alex: thanks all — let's try to keep the canary small and watch `slo.notify.estimated_cost_usd` closely.

sophie: Acked. I'll add the mock to the design board and link in the RFC.

jamal: will update RFC by EOD and assign reviewers.

alex: closing thread for now — follow-ups on RFC and dash tickets. :+1:
